Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

golemstockindices 0.1.0

  • First version: a ‘shiny’ app for exploring 44 major stock market indices of the US (S&P 500, Dow Jones, Nasdaq Composite, NYSE Composite, Russell 2000), the rest of the Americas (S&P/TSX Composite, Bovespa, IPC Mexico), Europe (STOXX Europe 600, Euro Stoxx 50, FTSE 100, DAX, CAC 40, IBEX 35, FTSE MIB, SMI, Euronext 100, BEL 20, AEX, ATX, ISEQ All Share, PSI, OMX Stockholm 30, OMX Copenhagen 25, OMX Helsinki 25, OSEBX, OMX Tallinn, OMX Riga, OMX Vilnius, Athens General, BIST 100) and Asia-Pacific (Nikkei 225, Shanghai Composite, Hang Seng, KOSPI, Taiwan Weighted, Sensex, Straits Times, ASX 200, All Ordinaries, NZX 50, IDX Composite, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI), and the VIX, with daily prices from Yahoo Finance and no API key. The Bovespa starts in 1995, after Brazil’s hyperinflation. Start it with run_app().
  • Tabs:
    • Overview shows which exchanges are open now and where every index stands (its last close with a line of its last year, the change on the day, this year and over a year, and how far it is below its all-time high). market_status(), index_summary() and overview_table() do the same from R.
    • Performance charts the indices side by side over a day, a week, 1, 3, 6 or 9 months, this year or a year, the best at the top. plot_performance() does the same from R.
    • Timeseries plots the whole history of an index as candles, with the volume, the 50- and 200-day moving averages and the drawdown.
    • Compare plots up to 10 indices from a chosen start date, each starting at 100, on a linear or log scale.
    • Returns calendar shows the monthly returns by year.
    • Seasonality asks whether some days of the week, weeks of the year, months or years of the US presidential cycle bring better returns than others, with a Kruskal-Wallis test of whether the differences could be chance.
    • Volatility says whether the volatility of the last weeks and the move of the last days are normal, against the index’s history and a GARCH(1,1) model, and forecasts the next 5 trading days with the value at risk.
    • Drawdowns says how far the index is below its all-time high and how long its earlier falls took to recover, with a chart and a table of the falls.
    • About explains what each index measures and how every number of the app is calculated.
  • Five more indices of Europe: FTSE 250, MDAX, SDAX, TecDAX and Next 150 (49 in all). Yahoo Finance has no history of the indices of Warsaw, Budapest and Reykjavik (only the last day), and its OMX Nordic 40 stops in 2015, so they are not included.
  • Six more indices: the Nasdaq-100, the FTSE All-Share, the FTSE/JSE Top 40 of South Africa, in a new Africa group, the Shenzhen Component, the Hang Seng China Enterprises and KOSDAQ (55 in all), with the exchanges of Johannesburg and Shenzhen in the strip of the Overview. Yahoo Finance has too little history of the MERVAL, the Tadawul, the CSI 300, the SET and the PSEi (from a day to a few months), and leaves out the Sunday sessions of Tel Aviv, so they are not included.
  • The prices of the indices are downloaded at the same time (8 requests at once) instead of one after the other, so the Overview opens in about 4 seconds the first time instead of 13, and in about 2 instead of 6 when the kept prices are more than an hour old.
  • The analysis code comes from golemcrypto, adapted to markets that close at weekends and on holidays: the windows count trading days, a year is 252 of them, a day’s return runs from the trading day before, and the forecast skips weekends.
  • The data, calculations and charts can be used directly from R: get_indices(), get_history(), index_summary(), normalize_prices(), monthly_returns(), seasonality_analysis(), volatility_analysis(), drawdown_analysis(), their *_text() functions, and the plot_*() and *_table() functions.
  • Each index’s history is downloaded once and kept on disk between R sessions; after an hour only its last two weeks are downloaded again. Set options(stockindices.cache_dir = ) to keep it elsewhere.
  • run_app(analytics = TRUE) adds Google Analytics, through the cookie banner of the sedzinfo.github.io sites, which loads it only after the visitor accepts; app.R turns it on for the public deployment.
